item.nusmp.collar_of_the_penitent_dragon:
Worn at the neck. Requires attunement. Special.
Bahamut's blessing: Radiant Breath (use): your breath weapon, as a bonus action: a cone of radiant light 6 blocks long that deals 6 holy damage to every foe in it (9 to the undead). 3% mana, cooldown ten seconds.
Penitent path: creatures of dragon kind (any creature with dragon, wyvern, drake or wyrm in its name that is not a great boss) recognise you and will not pick you as a target, unless you hurt them first. Tensura's holy attack resistance is lent to you.
Tabletop rules replaced: dragonborn and alignment requirements (dropped; any wearer may attune), the breath weapon (a Minecraft cone), advantage on Persuasion with dragons (they simply do not hunt you).
A silver collar with a dragon's head. Bahamut's blessing: use it to breathe a cone of radiant light, and dragons will not hunt you unless you wrong them. Holy damage is easier to bear.
item.nusmp.eye_of_the_aboleth.card:
Worn at the neck. No attunement. Special.
Charm (use): the creature you look at within 10 blocks (30 ft) must save (the Wisdom save is Tensura existence: it resists if its maximum EP is more than twice yours; great bosses always resist). If it fails, a creature is charmed for one minute: it will not pick you as a target and turns on the nearest monster within 12 blocks. A player is only dazed (Weakness II and Slowness for eight seconds). 2% mana, cooldown fifteen seconds.
item.nusmp.eye_of_the_aboleth.desc: A silver loop around a yellow slit-pupil eye. Use it on a creature within ten blocks: unless its will is far above yours it is charmed for a minute and will not strike you. A player is only dazed.
item.nusmp.fenrirs_collar.card:
Worn at the neck. Requires attunement. Unique.
The card's lycanthropy requirement is dropped (any wearer may attune): the wolf is the collar's own power.
Metamorphose (use): take the cursed hybrid form: +4 attack damage, +20% movement speed, +6 maximum health, +0.3 knockback resistance, night vision, Tensura's godwolf sense and strengthened body lent.
Under the full moon at night, or while a Moon Vigil still holds (until the next full moon), you keep control: the form lasts 5 minutes. At any other time the wolf is not yours: the form slips after 90 seconds and the curse takes its price (Weakness for 30 seconds).
Moon Vigil (sneak and use, once a day): a night at the full moon under the open sky. You heal 6 and Regeneration; until the next full moon (eight days) you hold the wolf.
Shed the Form (third ability): end the form at will, with no price.
Tabletop rules replaced: long rest (a day), the full moon (the moon phase of the world), "loss of control" (the cursed form's price).
item.nusmp.fenrirs_collar.desc: A crescent collar with a ruby. Use it to take the hybrid wolf form: stronger, faster, hardier, with a wolf's senses. At the full moon (or after a vigil under it) you keep your mind for five minutes; otherwise the wolf slips in ninety seconds and the curse takes its price.
item.nusmp.sunheart_medallion.card:
Worn at the neck. Requires attunement. Legend (can be a Djinn vessel).
Disease cannot take you: Tensura's infection is cured as it comes and poison resistance is lent. An evil wearer (one bound to a devil) burns: 4 fire damage every six seconds, never when it would leave them under three hearts.
The amulet holds 10 charges (kept per wearer; the count does not refill with the day). It is charged only by bathing in dawn's first light:
Greet the Dawn (use in the last 1500 ticks of the night or the first 1500 of the day, under the open sky, once a day): regain 1d8+3 charges, up to ten.
On command, Sacred Flame (use): 6 holy damage to the foe you look at (9 to the undead), no charge.
Charged powers (each pick by the Use Worn Relic key): Aura of Vitality (1 charge: Regeneration II for 20 seconds on you and friends within 10 blocks); Fire Shield (2: fire resistance and absorption for five minutes); Mass Cure Wounds (3: friends within 8 blocks heal 10); Greater Restoration (5: every harmful effect leaves you and friends within 6 blocks); Heal (6: 20 health to you or the friend you look at, and their harmful effects removed); Regenerate (7: 10 health and Regeneration III for a minute, and their harmful effects removed).
True Resurrection (sneak and use, once only): the amulet shatters into brilliant sunlight and is lost for ever. You and friends within 16 blocks are healed to full and carry a ward for ten minutes: the next blow that would kill each of them is nullified and leaves them on at least half their health.
Tabletop rules replaced: advantage on saves (cure and loan), 3d6 per round (4 every 6 seconds), 1d8+3 and the charge costs (kept exactly), spells (the nearest effects).
item.nusmp.sunheart_medallion.desc: A golden sun on a fine chain with ten charges, refilled by greeting dawn's first light. Sacred Flame on use; Vitality, Fire Shield, Mass Cure, Restoration, Heal and Regenerate spend charges; True Resurrection (once) shatters it. Disease cannot take you; the evil burn.
item.nusmp.witchers_medallion.card:
Worn at the neck. No attunement. Legend (can be a Djinn vessel).
The medallion alerts you of unusual events, monster presences and environmental influences, up to 20 blocks (20 m) away, and hums at the slightest threat: once a second it looks for monsters; when one comes near (or every five seconds while they stay) a line on your action bar tells you how many, how far the nearest is, and whether it lies ahead, behind, left or right; a great presence (a boss) makes it hum hard; a storm overhead makes it tremble. Tensura's danger sense and magic sense are lent to you.
Witcher Senses (use): for fifteen seconds you see in the dark, and every monster within 20 blocks glows. 2% mana, cooldown one minute.
item.nusmp.witchers_medallion.desc: A steel wolf's head with red eyes. It hums when monsters come within twenty blocks and tells you how many, how far and which way; it trembles before a storm and hums hard at a great presence. Use it for witcher senses: monsters glow for fifteen seconds.
item.nusmp.buffoons_pantaloons.card:
Worn at the belt. No attunement. Rare.
Gaudy and a little loose: +1 armour (the card's +1 AC), and advantage on athletic checks as a higher jump, a little more speed and a softer landing (+0.1 jump strength, +3% speed, +1 block of safe fall).
The price: every jump and every melee blow is a check, and one in twenty comes up a natural 1: the pantaloons fall down around your ankles. Until you spend an action pulling them up (use), you are slowed and weak (disadvantage on all checks).
item.nusmp.buffoons_pantaloons.desc: Gaudy baggy pantaloons: +1 armour and a spring in your step (higher jump, a little faster, softer landings). But a jump or a blow can come up a natural 1 and the pantaloons fall to your ankles: slow and weak until you spend an action pulling them up.
item.nusmp.executioners_bane.card:
Drunk and used up. Unique.
Drink it and for three hours of the day (3000 ticks) you survive being beheaded. In the game:
- A blow that would kill you leaves you on one hit point instead (with Resistance V for three seconds), once every ten seconds. A second killing blow inside those ten seconds is the head being destroyed and kills you as it would.
- The head still feels everything (Tensura's pain nullification is lent); but you are slowed and weakened, and you cannot eat or drink while it lasts.
- The head can be reattached: sleep through a night in a bed, or be cured by the Sunheart Medallion's Greater Restoration, Heal, Regenerate or Resurrection. The wound heals and the effect ends.
- If the three hours pass without that, the body gives out: you lose half your health (never the last point), and are slow and weak for a while. (The card says you die; nothing in this game kills outright.)
Tabletop rules replaced: head and body as separate targets, saving throw failures, spell and potion rules (dropped; the survival and its price are what is played).
item.nusmp.executioners_bane.desc: A black crystal vial on a gold chain. Drink it and for three hours of the day you survive being beheaded: a killing blow leaves you on one hit point (once every ten seconds). You are slow and weak and cannot eat or drink; sleep in a bed to put your head back, or the body gives out.
item.nusmp.perculiar_puking_poison.card:
Drunk and used up. Special.
Make a Constitution save (a d20 plus one for every four points of maximum health above 20, against 15; the card's DC 15). On a fail you are poisoned for one hour of the day (1000 ticks: Weakness all the while, Nausea at each puke) and about every ten minutes of it (167 ticks) you puke up something strange: six times, each a d20:
1 luminous rainbow slime (3 slimeballs, glowing); 2 a broom (a stick and wheat); 3 several large rocks (4 cobblestone); 4 acid (2 damage, corrosion or poison); 5 a live fish (a cod); 6 bubbles (water breathing, slow fall); 7 a book; 8 blood (1d4 damage, never the last point); 9 1d6 carrots; 10 a ship's anchor (2 iron ingots, 3 chains, slowness); 11 live ducklings (three baby chickens that go after two and a half minutes); 12 a well-crafted chair (oak stairs); 13 necrotic mush (rotten flesh); 14 a fist-sized ball of glass; 15 a large cactus (2); 16 a swarm of bugs (spider eyes, nausea); 17 deer antlers (bones); 18 a copy of your own head (your player head); 19 electrical plasma (4 lightning damage to every foe within 3 blocks, you slowed); 20 a full size coffin (a chest and a bone).
item.nusmp.perculiar_puking_poison.desc: A glass orb of swirling rainbow slime in a spiked claw. Drink it and make a Constitution save or be poisoned: six times, about every ten minutes of the hour, you puke up something strange (a broom, a chair, a coffin, a copy of your own head...).
item.nusmp.pocket_portal.card:
Very Rare potion (a glass orb), used up when it opens a portal.
Home Sweet Home: the orb remembers the circle it was brewed in. Sneak while you drink it to brew it where you stand (the orb you drink is swapped for a marked one; an orb never marked marks itself on first use). The portal always leads back to that spot, in the same world.
Smash the Orb (drink without sneaking): the orb breaks where you aim (up to twelve blocks, the ground in front of you if nothing is hit) and a ring of two blocks radius (the 10 ft portal) opens and stays for twelve seconds (two rounds, until the end of your next turn). Any creature that steps into the ring is carried to within a block of the circle (or the nearest free space) and cannot be carried again for three seconds. Bosses (300 health or more) are never carried. One portal per player at a time; it never changes a block. If the circle is in another world the portal will not open and the orb is kept.
Replaced: 'an action' = drinking the orb; 'permanent teleportation circle' = the spot marked by sneaking; 5 ft / 10 ft = 1 block / 2 blocks; 'end of your next turn' = 12 seconds.
item.nusmp.pocket_portal.desc: A glass orb of swirling purple. Sneak to brew it in the spot you stand; smash it elsewhere and a ring of light opens for twelve seconds that carries everyone who steps in back to that spot.
item.nusmp.potion_of_vampirism.card:
Very Rare potion. Drinking it rolls a d20 on the server, and the result is told to you.
1-12 Cursed (60%): for three Minecraft days (24000 ticks each) you gain a vampire's vulnerabilities: in sunlight (daytime, open sky, no rain) you take 1 damage a second and are weakened; in flowing water you take 1 damage a second; radiant, holy and sacred damage is doubled. These burns never take you below two hearts. Dying ends the curse.
13-18 Children of the Night (30%): for five Minecraft days, when a hostile creature wounds you, a pack answers (once in five minutes): 1d4 rounds later (6 to 24 seconds), wolves if you were under the open sky or bats (Tensura giant bats) if not arrive as your allies for five minutes. Their number is the card's 2d4 (bats) or 3d6 (wolves) halved and capped at six, the most summons a player may have. They fight what you fight and vanish if you die.
19-20 Regeneration (10%), for good: every other second you heal 3 health, but not while sunlight (daytime, open sky, no rain) or flowing water touches you, and not for a round (6 s) after you take radiant, holy or sacred damage. It is kept through death.
Replaced: 'vulnerabilities of a vampire (Monster Manual)' = sunlight, flowing water and double radiant damage; '3 days' / '5 days' = Minecraft days; 'summon 2d4 swarms / 3d6 wolves, arrive in 1d4 rounds, 1 hour' = the pack above (summon limit and five-minute cap); 'regain 20 hit points at the start of each turn' = 3 health every other second; 'radiant damage from running water, sunlight or holy water' = exposure to them or holy damage pauses it.
item.nusmp.potion_of_vampirism.desc: A skull-shaped flask with red eyes. Drink and roll a d20: most often a curse (sunlight and holy light burn you for three days), sometimes the Children of the Night (wolves and bats answer your wounds for five days), rarely Regeneration for good.
item.nusmp.romlos_potion_of_sleep.card:
Potion of unknown rarity (Special). Whoever drinks this falls asleep for five minutes unless they save.
Drink: you make the saving throw yourself. Sneak while you drink: you pour it into the mouth of the creature you face within four blocks (never a pet, a summon, or a creative or spectator player; players only where they can be harmed).
Wisdom save (DC 15): a d20 plus one per ten maximum health (at most ten) and up to three more for a full pool of magicules; a natural 20 always saves, a natural 1 never does. A creature that saves is only drowsy (Slowness) for ten seconds. One that fails sleeps for five minutes (the card's five hours at one minute an hour, since a sleeper is helpless): Tensura's Sleep effect, no movement, no fighting, no mining, no using items, and sleeping mobs pick no target. Any damage wakes it at once. A creature with 100 health or more only yawns (the potion is kept).
Replaced: 'DC 15 Wisdom saving throw' = the roll above; 'asleep for 5 hours' = 5 minutes.
item.nusmp.romlos_potion_of_sleep.desc: Bright lime liquid. Whoever drinks it must save or sleep for five minutes; sneak to pour it into the mouth of the creature in front of you. Damage wakes the sleeper.
item.nusmp.spider_brew.card:
Potion of unknown rarity (Special). Drink it and you morph into a giant spider for 1d4 'hours' (five minutes each, so 5 to 20 minutes), keeping your own mind.
Giant spider body: +6 maximum health (26 like the monster), +3 armour, +2 attack damage, a higher jump (+30%), a lower, longer body (scale 85%), night vision (darkvision).
Spider Climb: press yourself against any wall and you climb it; sneak to cling in place; no fall damage from the climb.
Poisonous bite: every melee hit you land poisons the target for six seconds, and a hit with an empty main hand (a bite) deals 3 more damage.
Tensura lends you Poison Resistance and Sticky Steel Thread (web) for the whole time, where the world has those skills. Drinking another Spider Brew while a spider only renews the time. Dying ends it.
Replaced: 'giant spider abilities' = the list above; 'keep your intelligence' = you keep your hands, items, chat and spells; 1d4 hours = 1d4 x 5 minutes; Web Walker is not reproduced (cobwebs still slow you).
item.nusmp.spider_brew.desc: A bottle of blue liquid wrapped in cobweb. Drink to become a giant spider for five to twenty minutes with your own mind: climb walls, a poisonous bite, more health and armour, night vision.
item.nusmp.hand_of_vecna.card:
Artifact (God grade), worn in the Hands slot, requires attunement. In the tabletop rules you cut off your left hand and press the Hand to the stump; here the five-second attunement ritual is the cutting, and the first second it works for you it GRAFTS: it cannot be taken off while you live (Curios refuses; an operator frees you with /vecna release <player>; your death frees it and it drops). The game has no alignment: the evil of the Hand is its Whisper.
Strength 20: +7 attack damage, +3 armor and +2 armor toughness while it is worn.
Cold blows: every melee blow adds 3 cold damage (1.5 on a player) and a few seconds of Tensura frost and slowness.
Touch of Death (3% existence points, 60 s cooldown): the creature you touch takes 20 heavy damage and Wither II; a player takes at most 45% of their health and is never left under a heart.
Rimed Grasp (5% mana, 30 s): every foe within six blocks takes 7 cold damage, frost, Slowness III and freezing.
Skeleton to Jelly (needs the Eye too; 4% existence points, 5 min): the touched creature loses 30% of its maximum health (10% on a boss; a player at most 45%, never below a heart), then Slowness III, Weakness III and Glowing.
Coercion: after any Hand act there is a 20% chance of Vecna's Whisper: 8 seconds of Mining Fatigue and a whisper in chat. It takes nothing from you and never forces an act.
The pair of Vecna (Hand and Eye both worn and attuned to one bearer): immune to poison and disease (poison, hunger, magicule poison and infection are cleansed every second, and Poison Resistance, Paralysis Resistance and Danger Sense are lent); cannot be surprised (the first blow from an attacker in each 20 seconds is turned aside); regeneration of one health every two seconds; safe X-ray (no magicule cost); Skeleton to Jelly and the Wish can be used.
The Wish (the pair): Choose the Wish cycles Full Restore, A Day of Resilience, Clear Skies, Summon Rain; Make the Wish grants the chosen one, once in 30 real days for each player.
item.nusmp.hand_of_vecna.desc: A withered grey hand in an ornate gold gauntlet. Attuning grafts it to your wrist for as long as you live: strength of a giant, cold in every blow, and a whisper that wants you to do evil. Worn with the Eye, it is more.
item.nusmp.eye_of_vecna.card:
Artifact (God grade), worn on the Head, requires attunement. In the tabletop rules you gouge out your eye and press the Eye into the socket; here the five-second attunement ritual is the pressing, and the first second it works for you it GRAFTS: it carries the curse of binding and cannot be taken off while you live (an operator frees you with /vecna release <player>; your death frees it and it drops).
Sight: lends Eye of Truth and Farsight, night vision, and X-ray: every second, mobs and players within 24 blocks that you cannot see glow through the walls (it costs a sliver of magicules unless the pair is worn).
Clairvoyance (4% mana, 60 s): names the five nearest living things within 96 blocks with their coordinates, and makes them glow for ten seconds.
Crown of Madness (3% mana, 45 s): the mob you look at (not a boss) fights its own allies for ten seconds.
Disintegrate (3% existence points, 60 s): a grey beam of 26 heavy damage; it removes no block; a player takes at most 45% of their health and is never left under a heart.
Dominate Monster (6% mana, 2 min): the mob you look at (not a boss, not a player) is your ally for one minute.
Eyebite (3% mana, 30 s): a cone twelve blocks long of Tensura fear, Weakness II and Slowness II for ten seconds (four on a player).
Vecna's Hunger: each use of the Eye has a 5% chance of it: for 20 seconds you are in darkness and slowed and a spectral hand hunts you alone. Kill it. It cannot take your last heart, drops nothing, and never takes control of you or locks you out.
The pair of Vecna (Hand and Eye both worn and attuned to one bearer): immune to poison and disease (poison, hunger, magicule poison and infection are cleansed every second, and Poison Resistance, Paralysis Resistance and Danger Sense are lent); cannot be surprised (the first blow from an attacker in each 20 seconds is turned aside); regeneration of one health every two seconds; safe X-ray (no magicule cost); Skeleton to Jelly and the Wish can be used.
item.nusmp.eye_of_vecna.desc: A pink-irised eye on a red cord. Attuning presses it into your socket for as long as you live: it sees through walls and in the dark, casts five terrible spells, and sometimes, one use in twenty, hungers for you. Worn with the Hand, it is more.
item.nusmp.deck_of_many_things.card:
Artifact (God grade), a charm, no attunement. A deck of 22 cards. Draw One, Two or Three Cards: you draw exactly the number you chose, at most three a game day, and never more than the deck holds; the deck is shuffled once (the great and terrible cards tend to lie deeper) and the 22 are drawn without repeat. After the 22nd card the deck crumbles to dust. Look at the Deck shows how many are left and which have been drawn.
Nothing in the deck kills, takes a relic or a ledger item, or locks you out of the game. The cards: Balance (harmful effects cleansed, Resistance for 5 min); Comet (the next hostile monster you kill alone within a day gives 3 levels); The Donjon (3 minutes of Slowness II, Weakness and Mining Fatigue in a ring of dark glass); Euryale (30 minutes of bad luck and weakness); The Fates (misfortunes lifted, Luck II for 10 min); Flames (an Infernal Envoy, a wither skeleton, hunts you for a minute); The Fool (lose 3 levels, the deck draws again); Gem (25 emeralds); Idiot (10 minutes of Mining Fatigue and Weakness); Jester (4 levels, or two more cards, fixed by the deck); Key (a random unissued RARE relic weapon, ledger-stamped; a pair gives both halves; diamonds if none is left); Knight (an iron golem ally for 5 minutes); Moon (one to three boons for 10 minutes); Rogue (a vindicator, The Turncoat, hunts you for a minute); Ruin (up to 64 emeralds and magic stones lost, bad luck for 10 minutes); Skull (an Avatar of Death, a vex, hunts you for 90 seconds); Star (for good: +1 heart and +1 attack damage, at most three times); Sun (a random unissued UNIQUE relic and 6 levels); Talons (half a stack, at most 32, of a plain valuable or food is torn up; never a relic, a tool or enchanted gear); Throne (Hero of the Village and Absorption for a day, 16 gold, the title Lord of the Keep); Vizier (names the nearest Labyrinth Spire if you are in the Labyrinth, or the nearest Dungeon Gate in the Overworld); The Void (2 minutes of Slowness IV, blindness and Resistance V: you cannot move or see, and nothing can harm you).
The hostile summons last at most 90 seconds, fight only you, drop nothing, and can never take your last heart.
item.nusmp.deck_of_many_things.desc: Twenty-two cards in a gold-edged case. Choose how many to draw (one, two or three a day) and you draw exactly that many: wonders and ruin, nothing that kills and nothing that takes a relic. After the twenty-second the deck crumbles to dust.
item.nusmp.the_infinity_gauntlet.card:
Artifact (Genesis grade), worn in the Hands slot, requires attunement. Any Infinity Stone you carry anywhere on you (inventory or Curios) is set in the Gauntlet and answers through it; the Gauntlet must be worn. Each carried Stone makes the Stones' acts 12% stronger (range, time, damage), up to +72% with all six, and a worn Gauntlet lends the skills of the Space, Mind, Time and Soul Stones and the pool doubling of the Power Stone even if the Stones are only carried. (The card's rule that the Gauntlet's bearer cannot attune other items is replaced by the usual limit of three attuned relics; the Stones themselves need no attunement slot.)
Greater Wish (all six Stones carried, once a game day): Choose the Wish cycles Treasure (32 diamonds and 32 emeralds), Restoration (every player and pet of yours within 48 blocks healed to full and cleansed), Resistance (Resistance II, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing for 10 minutes), Immunity (cleansed now and every second for a day), Reroll (the blow you took in the last six seconds is healed back).
The Snap (all six Stones carried, once a game day, 10% existence points): every hostile mob within 48 blocks loses half of its current health (a boss a tenth of its maximum), is weakened and slowed, never to zero; no player is touched and no block is changed. The bearer pays with 30 seconds of Weakness II and Mining Fatigue II.
Acts: Space, Mind, Power, Time, Reality, Soul Stone (each needs its Stone carried).
item.nusmp.the_infinity_gauntlet.desc: A black gauntlet with a ribcage palm and six sockets. Every Infinity Stone you carry is set in it and answers through it, stronger for each; with all six it makes the Greater Wish and the Snap, once a day each.
item.nusmp.the_space_stone_or_the_tesser: The Space Stone, or the Tesseract

Artifact (God grade), a charm. Lends Spatial Motion while worn.
Tesseract (3% mana, 60 s): you and up to nine willing companions (players who are sneaking, pets of yours) within 12 blocks step to your marked place on the same plane (the dimension). With no mark, to your bed or the world spawn. The card's save for unwilling people is replaced by consent: only those who sneak are taken.
Mark the Place (sneak and use): marks where you stand as the destination in this dimension.
A small blue cube of folded space. Mark a place (sneak and use), then step to it with up to nine willing companions. It lends you Spatial Motion.
item.nusmp.the_mind_stone.card:
Artifact (God grade), a charm. Lends Thought Communication and Analytical Appraisal while worn.
Sense Minds (30 s): lists, with coordinates and what they are about to do, the nearest twelve thinking creatures (players, villagers, illagers, piglins, witches) within 200 blocks, and makes those within 96 glow for five seconds.
Read Mind (sneak and use, 5 s): learns what the creature you look at is, holds and wants. A player resists on a d20 + 0 against DC 20 (only a natural 20).
item.nusmp.the_mind_stone.desc: A small yellow gem that hears. Use it to sense every thinking creature within two hundred blocks; sneak and use to read the mind in front of you. It lends you Thought Communication and Analytical Appraisal.
item.nusmp.the_power_stone.card:
Artifact (God grade), a charm. Doubles your pools: maximum magicules and maximum aura +50% and magicule regeneration +100% (Tensura attributes; no new stat). The card's doubling of uses per day is replaced by this doubling of the pools.
Power Burst (2% existence points, 45 s): a shock of power: every foe within six blocks takes 14 heavy damage and is thrown back.
item.nusmp.the_power_stone.desc: A small purple gem of raw power. Your magicule and aura pools swell by half and refill twice as fast; use it for a shock of power that throws back every foe round you.
item.nusmp.the_time_stone_or_the_eye_of_: The Time Stone, or the Eye of Agamotto

Artifact (God grade), a charm. Lends Danger Sense while worn.
Foresight (a ritual: hold use for five seconds; 2 min cooldown): for 600 seconds (twelve thousand ticks) the first blow from an attacker in each 20 seconds is turned aside, Luck II is yours, and Tensura future vision shows you what is to come for two minutes. The tabletop's advantage on rolls is replaced by the luck and the guard.

A small green gem that sees what is to come. Hold use to cast Foresight as a ritual: for twelve thousand ticks you cannot be surprised, luck is with you and the future is in sight. It lends you Danger Sense.
item.nusmp.the_reality_stone.card:
Artifact (God grade), a charm.
Polymorph (3% mana, 30 s): the mob you look at (not a boss, not a player) is made small (40% size, where Tensura's size attributes exist), weak (Weakness III) and slow for thirty seconds. The card's swap into another creature, and polymorphing objects, are replaced by this reversible shrinking.
Seeming (sneak and use, 3% mana, 60 s): invisible and hard to sense for three minutes.
Mirage Arcane (3% mana, 30 s): foes within 14 blocks lose their target and stumble for ten seconds (Greater Image and Mirage Arcane in one).
item.nusmp.the_reality_stone.desc: A small red gem that rewrites. Polymorph shrinks and weakens a mob in sight; sneak and use for Seeming (unseen for three minutes); the Mirage makes nearby foes lose you.
item.nusmp.the_soul_stone.card:
Artifact (God grade), a charm. True sight at any distance: lends Eye of Truth while worn.
Anyone who dies within 64 blocks of you has their soul stored in the Stone (twelve at most; the names of players are kept). True Resurrection (automatic, once a game day, needs a stored soul): a killing blow that would end you instead leaves you on half your health with Regeneration III, Resistance II and Absorption. Count the Souls shows what the Stone holds. (The card's resurrection of another person, and keeping the dead from being raised, are replaced by this return of the bearer.)
item.nusmp.the_soul_stone.desc: A small orange gem that keeps the dead. You see truly at any distance; the souls of those who die within sixty-four blocks are stored in it, and once a day one of them brings you back from a killing blow.
item.nusmp.paradox.card:
Artifact staff (God grade), requires attunement. +3 damage and 2d4 more on every melee blow (the card's 2d10 scaled to a Minecraft blow; half of that on a player) and a critical blow (x1.5) on 19 or 20 of a d20.
Twenty charges, refilled by 2d8+4 at each dawn (a long or short rest). Acts (sneak-use picks the second): Slow (3 charges: foes within 10 blocks, Slowness III and Weakness); Phase Lock (5: the creature you look at is held, for as long as the control caps allow: 5 s on a mob, 3 s on a player, 1 s on a boss); Phase Stasis (3: the same for a person: a player, villager, illager, piglin or witch); Temporal Movement (3: Speed II and Haste II for 15 s); Time Stop (9: every foe within 16 blocks is held, you move at Speed III); Alternate Reality (3: foes within 18 blocks lose their target and stumble for 5 s); Turn the Clock (1: the damaged item in your off hand is turned back to new; not a relic); Missing Time (3: everyone within 18 blocks, you included, saves against DC 15 or is aged (slow and weak) or made young (regenerating and quick) for 20 s).
The Paradox: Time Stop and Missing Time force the staff: you save against DC 17 (d20, only a 17 or more holds); on a failure you are cast out of the timeline back to where you stood about ten seconds ago, tired (Slowness), and the madness table rolls: 0 you are knocked flat; 1-49 short-term (nausea and slowness for 1d10 x 10 s); 50-99 long-term (5 minutes of nausea, weakness and mining fatigue); 100 indefinite (10 minutes, or until milk). The staff's sentience and its habit of vanishing into the timeline are not played.
item.nusmp.paradox.desc: The staff of the God of Time: a twisted thorn of violet crystal. Its blows carry extra weight and a critical on 19 and 20; twenty charges, refilled by 2d8+4 each dawn, buy slows, holds, haste, a stopped moment, a turned clock and missing years. Forcing it may cast you out of your own timeline.
item.nusmp.warrens_key.card:
Artifact (God grade), a charm, no attunement. It never works inside the Labyrinth or the Living Dungeon, whose doors are not to be changed.
Knock and Arcane Lock (a shared pool of five uses a game day; spent only when the spell works): Knock opens the door, gate, trapdoor or chest you point at and lifts your own arcane lock from it; Arcane Lock shuts and locks it against everyone but you (sixteen locks at most, kept with the world, until you knock them away).
Door to Door (five a game day): the door you point at and a door the Key remembers (it learns every door it touches, twelve at most; Choose the Door cycles which) become the two ends of a portal on the same plane that stays open for an hour, or until either door is shut: step into one doorway and you come out of the other (walk-through, one second apart). If the Key knows no other door on this plane, the spell fails. The tabletop's plane shift and teleport accuracy are replaced by this remembered-door rule.
item.nusmp.warrens_key.desc: A long bronze skeleton key with a labyrinth for a bit. Five a day it knocks or arcane-locks a door, gate, trapdoor or chest; five a day it joins the door in front of you to a door it remembers, as a portal that stays open an hour. It does not work inside the Dungeon.
effect.nusmp.soul_corruption.description: Lucius's Soul Touch has cut into your soul: maximum health is reduced by 10% per level (three levels, never below four hearts) for a minute. A new touch adds a level. Milk or a Totem of Undying cleanses it.
effect.nusmp.paladin.description: Purified by Lucius Zogratis's Paladin Conversion: this creature serves its caster with doubled health, 60% more attack, 8 armour, 4 toughness and 15% more speed, wears a halo and wings of light, and never harms its master.
nusmp.page.book_shadow.shadow_travel: Shadow Travel - slip into the shadow you stand in and rise from the shadow you aim at (or the nearest one ahead). Both spots must be dark (light level 3 or less). Costs more the further you go; up to two sneaking allies follow.
nusmp.page.book_shadow.unite_equus: Unite Mode: Equus - united with Slotos, the horse devil: +10 armor, +6 toughness, 40% less physical damage, no knockback, 25% slower, for 30 s. (Nacht Faust's grimoire only.)
nusmp.page.book_shadow.unite_felis: Unite Mode: Felis - united with Plumede, the cat devil: +30% speed, higher jumps, night sight, 20% dodge, mobs beyond 8 blocks lose you, living things within 24 blocks are outlined for you alone. (Nacht Faust's grimoire only.)
nusmp.page.book_shadow.unite_gallus_call: Gallus: Walgner's Call - while united with Gallus: the first call stuns every enemy within 8 blocks (1.5 to 2.5 s); the second roots the enemy you look at for 4 s. (Nacht Faust's grimoire only.)
nusmp.page.book_butoh.butoh_dance: Kiato's dance, now a passive: anyone who holds Butoh Magic dances by themselves, with no need to cast it. You move in a flowing, never-repeating dance: eight moves in an order only the dance knows. While it lasts, a blow aimed at you may find nobody there (35 to 65 percent by the move you are in, at most 65 percent, 20 points less against bosses; falls, fire, poison and the void are never dodged), a dodge slips you one step aside and leaves an ink after-image, your body is 15 to 25 percent smaller (a harder target), and Butoh pages you cast hit for 15 percent more. It costs mana every second (1 percent of your maximum, half of that while you stand still) and stops when you run dry (it returns once you have 15 percent of your mana again), are stunned, asleep, frozen in time, riding, swimming or gliding, and it comes back by itself afterwards. Casting this page costs nothing: it only switches the dance between resting and dancing.
nusmp.page.book_butoh.butoh_dash_deflect: A quick dash along the way you are moving (or the way you look), 5.5 blocks, 6.5 while dancing. For 12 ticks afterwards every arrow, bolt or fireball that reaches you is turned around at its shooter, with you as its new owner, so it can hurt the one who sent it. While dancing the return is faster and tighter. A missile can be turned back twice at most. About 6 seconds to recharge.
effect.nusmp.relic_nullified.description: A spatial pulse has de-attuned every relic you carry. They stay equipped and stay yours; they simply do not answer until this ends.
effect.nusmp.severed.description: Your Djinn and your Black Clover spirits are cut off from you. Nothing is lost: they answer again when this ends.
effect.nusmp.time_decay.description: Lucius's aura stops all passive healing here: natural regeneration, the Regeneration effect and regeneration skills. Healing potions and food still work.
nusmp.page.book_soul_corpse.corpse_reani: Raises Soul Zombies at your side (up to 2 for the dead of the last minute; when no one has died near you the earth gives up one to three, each for a little mana). They are real zombies that obey you: they follow you, fight your foes only, never burn in daylight and drop nothing. They last about a minute. You own at most six zombies at once (the oldest is dismissed first). This page is open from the start.
item.nusmp.zogratis_hourglass.tip.lore: The sand falls upward for those who are ready to meet him.
item.nusmp.zogratis_hourglass.tip.use: Hold right click for 3 seconds: you and every player within 8 blocks (party first) are carried to Lucius's arena. Hold again inside to go home.
item.nusmp.zogratis_hourglass.tip.rules: Not in the Labyrinth or the dungeons. Not while hurt, nor while Lucius fights (leaving mid-fight takes 10 seconds). 60 second cooldown after coming home.
advancement.nusmp.root.title: Multiverse of Anime
advancement.nusmp.root.desc: Grimoires, relics and dungeons of many worlds. Every spell you cast and every foe you fell is written down here.
advancement.nusmp.start.first_grimoire.d: Receive your grimoire, the book that will carry your magic.
advancement.nusmp.start.open_book.title: Open the Cover
advancement.nusmp.start.open_book.desc: Open your grimoire and read its first pages.
advancement.nusmp.start.ceremony.title: The Acceptance Ceremony
advancement.nusmp.start.ceremony.desc: Take part in the Grimoire Acceptance Ceremony and let a grimoire choose you.
advancement.nusmp.start.questionnaire.de: Answer every question of the Tower Wizard and learn which magic is born in you.
advancement.nusmp.start.meet_wizard.desc: Speak with the wizard of a Grimoire Tower.
advancement.nusmp.start.first_spell.desc: Cast a spell from your grimoire.
advancement.nusmp.start.mana_use.title: Spending Mana
advancement.nusmp.start.mana_use.desc: Cast twenty-five spells. Every spell costs mana, and mana refills slowly.
advancement.nusmp.start.casts_50.title: Practice Makes Perfect
advancement.nusmp.start.casts_50.desc: Cast fifty spells. Mastery comes from successful casts.
advancement.nusmp.start.casts_500.title: Tireless Caster
advancement.nusmp.start.first_page.title: A New Page
advancement.nusmp.start.first_page.desc: Unlock a new page of your grimoire through mastery.
advancement.nusmp.start.pages_5.title: Five Pages Deep
advancement.nusmp.start.pages_10.title: A Full Grimoire
advancement.nusmp.start.pages_10.desc: Unlock ten pages: a grimoire that has grown with its master.
advancement.nusmp.start.mastery.title: Mastery
advancement.nusmp.start.mastery.desc: Fill the mastery bar of a grimoire completely.
advancement.nusmp.start.magic_stone.desc: Pick up a magic stone, the dungeon's currency.
advancement.nusmp.start.five_grimoires.d: Receive five grimoires over your journeys.
advancement.nusmp.magic.awakening.title: The Awakening of Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.awakening.desc: Cast three spells and let the world learn your name.
advancement.nusmp.magic.soul_flame.title: Flame Soul
advancement.nusmp.magic.soul_flame.desc: Cast any magic of the Flame Soul (fire, blast and molten stone).
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_flame.title: Flame Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_flame.desc: Cast a spell of Flame Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_explosion.d: Cast a spell of Explosion Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_magma.title: Magma Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_magma.desc: Cast a spell of Magma Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_ash.title: Ash Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_ash.desc: Cast a spell of Ash Magic.
Cast a signature page of any magic of the Flame Soul.
advancement.nusmp.magic.master_flame.des: Cast every magic of the Flame Soul at least once (4 in all).
advancement.nusmp.magic.soul_water.title: Water Soul
advancement.nusmp.magic.soul_water.desc: Cast any magic of the Water Soul (tides, frost, mist and silver).
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_water.title: Water Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_water.desc: Cast a spell of Water Magic.

advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_ice.desc: Cast a spell of Ice Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_mercury.des: Cast a spell of Mercury Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_mist.title: Mist Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_mist.desc: Cast a spell of Mist Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_gel.title: Gel Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_gel.desc: Cast a spell of Gel Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_bubble.desc: Cast a spell of Bubble Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_ice_wedge.d: Cast a spell of Ice Wedge Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_mucus.title: Mucus Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_mucus.desc: Cast a spell of Mucus Magic.

advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_snow.desc: Cast a spell of Snow Magic.
Cast a signature page of any magic of the Water Soul.
advancement.nusmp.magic.master_water.des: Cast every magic of the Water Soul at least once (9 in all).
advancement.nusmp.magic.soul_wind.title: Wind Soul
advancement.nusmp.magic.soul_wind.desc: Cast any magic of the Wind Soul (gales, stars, storms and wings).
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_wind.title: Wind Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_wind.desc: Cast a spell of Wind Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_star.title: Star Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_star.desc: Cast a spell of Star Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_storm.title: Storm Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_storm.desc: Cast a spell of Storm Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_air.title: Air Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_air.desc: Cast a spell of Air Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_sound.title: Sound Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_sound.desc: Cast a spell of Sound Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_vortex.desc: Cast a spell of Vortex Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_wing.title: Wing Magic
advancement.nusmp.magic.cast_wing.desc: Cast a spell of Wing Magic.
advancement.nusmp.magic.signature_wind.d: Cast a signature page of any magic of the Wind Soul.
advancement.nusmp.magic.master_wind.desc: Cast every magic of the Wind Soul at least once (7 in all).

message.nusmp.mega.mhb.travel.arrive: Floor 0, the Sanctuary. Nothing here wishes you harm. The Spire to the east climbs, the Chasm to the west descends; the gate behind you leads home.
message.nusmp.mega.mhb.travel.leave: The Sanctuary lets you go. The gate stands quiet behind you.
message.nusmp.mega.mhb.travel.no_level: The Sanctuary does not answer: its dimension is not loaded.

message.nusmp.mega.crucible.collapse: The ceiling groans. Watch the floor and RUN!
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.crumble: The other relics crumble to dust.
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.empty_slot: There is nothing on this pedestal.
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.exhausted: The pedestals stay bare: every relic of this rank already walks the world.

message.nusmp.mega.crucible.refused: The Order's ledger refuses: that relic walks the world already. The vault falls silent.
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.road: The relic chooses the road: the next ten floors are %s.
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.spirit: A Cursed Spirit tears itself out of the stone!
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.swapped: Another hand had claimed that relic: a different one took its place.
message.nusmp.mega.crucible.too_late: Too late: a relic was already taken and the others are dust.

advancement.nusmp.dungeon.mega_gear.desc: Find a graded piece of standard gear in the Mega-Dungeon.
advancement.nusmp.dungeon.mega_gear_rare: Find a Rare-grade piece of standard gear, made to turn magic aside.

arc.dialogue._fallback.1: Ah, %1$s. I do not think we have met. I am %2$s.
arc.dialogue._fallback.5: The road ahead is long, %1$s. Do not rush it.
arc.dialogue._fallback.6: A door that will not open usually has another way around.
arc.dialogue._fallback.7: You have already brought one of them down. Keep your head, and keep going.
arc.dialogue._fallback.8: Every story starts with a first fight. Choose it well.
item.nusmp.genesis_core.desc1: Take it to a Soul Forge to design an Avatar. It is spent only when the Avatar is born.
item.nusmp.soul_forge.desc1: Place it, hold a Genesis Core and use it: the ritual of the Avatar begins.
item.nusmp.soul_forge.desc2: Each Avatar costs one Genesis Core. The forge itself is never used up.

message.nusmp.mega.enc.celestial_court.c: The sentence has been passed. The executioner is on its way.
Two halves of the golden gate swing shut behind a sentinel's step.
The statues between the columns have not been there as long as you thought.
The court sits in judgement on the unlit. The condemned are called.
The host of the court has come down from the terraces.
A horn from the terrace. The host has been summoned, and you are why.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.holy_church.churc: The bell tolls once, and something in the belfry gets up.
A tomb lid slides aside in the side chapel. Armour that was knighted here stands up.
Stone grinds above you. The gargoyles on the buttresses have turned their heads.
Chanting from the apse, in a tongue the church does not use.
The procession of the crypt has begun, and you are the way it is walking.
The great bell tolls and every candle in the nave leans toward you.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.mountain_monaster: The gate guardian has heard you coming and is not going to move aside.
The great gong has been struck, and not by anyone friendly.
Something is moving inside the paper walls.
A gong, and the rogue monks form a ring. A challenge has been called.
The mountain has decided against you, and it brought company.
You hear nothing, which is how you know he is there.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sky_citadel.sky_g: A horn for the giants' table, and you are what is being served.
Something very large stirs in a chair built for it.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sky_citadel.sky_s: Every curtain on the gallery stands out sideways at once.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sky_citadel.sky_t: Thunder rolls down the gallery from the wrong direction.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sky_citadel.sky_w: The wind in the arched windows has found a voice and a direction.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.celestial_c: Marble terraces under an open sky, and a court that has been waiting for you to be tried.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.holy_church: Candles gutter in the nave, and the bell has not been rung by a living hand in a long time.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.mountain_mo: Paper lanterns, bamboo and a bell on the mountain wind: the discipline of this place went wrong in a quiet way.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.sky_citadel: Everything here was built for something ten times your size, and the floor ends where the cloud begins.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.feywild_gro: Giant flowers glow where no sun reaches, and every path you take was chosen for you by something that is laughing.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.dwarven_for: The hearths were never banked, and a hammer still rings in the great hall with nobody swinging it.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.crystal_geo: The whole room is one crystal, humming, and each of your footsteps comes back from a different wall.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.sunken_temp: A kind god's temple, flooded to the knee, where the lanterns still burn under the water and the hymn goes on.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.sat: Pipes and hooves on the turf, and a laugh with an edge on it. The feast has no seat for you.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.wil: Small lights drift out of the dark, and each one is pretending to be the way out.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.bri: The hedge beside you rustles, and whatever is in it has too many legs.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.hag: A crone hums over a pot that was not there a moment ago. She has a bargain for you, and her friends are listening.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.wil: A horn, far off, then much nearer. The Wild Hunt is riding through the grove and you are on its road.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.bra: The thickets close in. Every hedge around you has something in it, and all of it is moving.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.feywild_grove.mid: Midsummer: a whole revel spills out of the flowers, laughing, and the guest of honour is you.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.dwarven_forgehold: Grey beards and grey axes come down the long hall. The hold's rebels do not keep a guest room.
The vein in the wall shivers. Something has been eating the ore from the inside, and it has come out.
An anvil rings once with nobody at it. The armour on the racks stands up, and the forges answer.
Drums from the lower deeps and a great many boots on the stair. The horde has found the hold's front door.
A horn in the great hall, and the whole hold turns out in arms: the golem, the armour and the fire.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.cry: A facet in the wall opens like an eye. Then another, and another.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.ech: A geode carries every step a long way. Wings answer from all the galleries at once.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.umb: The wall beside you hums, then splits. Something with horns has been tunnelling toward the sound of you.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.liv: Two of the crystal statues were never statues. Their facets turn, slowly, toward you.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.cub: The floor shivers, and slimes full of light well up between the shells with sparks riding on them.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.sha: A wall sheds its crystal in a hundred pieces, and the pieces have teeth.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.crystal_geode.geo: The geode groans, a wall comes down with a roar, and what it was hiding steps through while the floor is still ringing.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sunken_temple.los: A bell under the water, and singing. The temple's dead are at their hymn, and you are quiet enough to hear it.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sunken_temple.col: The statue of the god turns its head. Water streams from its shoulders, and it begins to walk.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sunken_temple.dee: Something in the cisterns has noticed that you carry no light, and it is coming up the stairs.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sunken_temple.flo: The pool is rising, and the water has teeth. The tide has come in and it brought company.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.sunken_temple.dro: The bell sounds, the hymn begins, and the whole drowned congregation rises to sing you down.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.cursed_archive.ca: Chains rattle on the aisle ahead. The censors have come for what you are carrying.
A cough, from every shelf at once. The rule of the room is silence, and you have not kept it.
The ink on the nearest page lifts off the paper and learns to fly.
Something in the aisle says your name, and says it is overdue.
A bay of shelving tips toward you, and something steps out from behind it.
A page turns by itself, and then every page in the room.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.haunted_manor.hm_: The air in front of you is colder than the room.
Every door in the house opens at once.
Someone has come downstairs in a gown. She was not expecting company, and she is not pleased.
A music box, somewhere, playing a tune you almost know.
A chair slides across the floor, and nobody pushed it.
The armour on the wall is facing the other way than it was.
Doors slam all over the house, one after another, toward you.
A cauldron lid clatters, and a voice says dinner is nearly ready.
Strings, out of tune, and the sound of many feet on the boards.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.necropolis.nc_bon: The bones in the wall have been gathered. Something has put them together.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.necropolis.nc_bur: The ground gives, and the ones under it have been awake a long time.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.necropolis.nc_dea: Armour, and the iron sound of an oath being kept, coming up out of the tomb.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.necropolis.nc_gna: The niches in the wall are not all full any more.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.necropolis.nc_oss: Every skull in the wall turns the same way, and it is yours.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.necropolis.nc_pro: A bell, slow and far off. Then footsteps in step, coming this way.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.vampire_castle.vc: The bell rings once, and the belfry empties.
The hunt has your scent, and the whole court has heard you coming.
Lids slide across the floor, from every side.
A coffin lid slides to the floor. Then the next.
Stone grinds above you. The gargoyles on the roof have turned their heads.
A howl in the yard, and then many of them, closer.
Someone is standing in the mirror who is not standing beside you.
A gentleman in evening dress bows to you from the stair. He does not cast a shadow.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.cursed_arch: Chained books climb out of sight, and the quiet here is not peace, it is a rule that somebody enforces.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.haunted_man: Dust sheets, a music box, and a house that still keeps the hour it ended; every room is as the family left it, and not everybody left.
A city of the dead laid out in streets and squares, where every door is a tomb and the lamps were never allowed to go out.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.vampire_cas: A castle that keeps its own night: red velvet, a mirror that shows the room but not you, and a host who has expected you for some time.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.fungal_unde: Spores drift where no sun ever came, and every cap you pass is listening.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.infernal_fo: Everything here is on shift, and every bargain is already signed.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.drowned_cry: The sea took the church and kept the congregation.
message.nusmp.mega.mgd.theme.spider_warr: White silk over black stone; something very large has been waiting for guests.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.drowned_crypt.dc_: A bell rings, a long way down.
Water running off something that is walking.
The water in the hall is rising.
The lid of the tomb is on the floor.
Someone is singing, under the water.
Boots, a great many, on the stairs.
A voice in a language that is not for you.
Soft footsteps, and eight legs behind them.
Something round and unblinking is hanging in the dark.
The mushrooms shiver all at once.
Lights go out, one at a time, in a ring.
The spores go off like a drum.
Something lets go of the cap above you.
Two armies have found the same corridor.
The air shimmers; something small is laughing.
Every door in the foundry has opened.
The armour on the rack is still hot.
Somebody has rung for the crew.
Claws on iron plates, coming fast.
message.nusmp.mega.enc.spider_warrens.sw: Something has let go of the ceiling.
Someone is whistling to the spiders.
Every web in the warren is shaking.
The guard has been told you are here.
Eight legs on stone, many times over.
The threads are all pulled at once.
message.nusmp.mega.party.entry.solo: You walk the floors of your own: a party of one. Join an FTB team to share them with friends.
message.nusmp.mega.party.entry.team: Your party %s has floors of its own. %s of you are in the dungeon now.
message.nusmp.mega.party.evicted: These floors belong to another party. The dungeon sends you back to the Hub; go in again by your own gate.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.1: Charlotte Roselei, Blue Rose. Do not stare. State your business or leave.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.2: Hmph. Another delver. Keep your distance and your hands to yourself, and we will get along.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.3: You are not unbearable. That is rare. Go on, speak.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.4: You are the one clearing the guardian floors? ...Fine. I suppose that earns you a place within arm's reach.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.6: Back again? Do not make a habit of it. ...Do.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.7: Thorns exist so that nobody has to apologise for what they protect. Remember that when you build a defence.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.8: A trap you have seen is half-defused. The dungeon is full of them. Look at the floor before you step on it.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.9: Briars bind what they touch. Fire frees you, so does a sharp blade, so does patience. Panic is the only thing that does not.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.10: If you happen to meet the Black Bulls' captain, you did not hear my name from me.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.11: Take your party's weakest member seriously. A chain breaks at its smallest link, and a squad at its most careless knight.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.12: Noise and light draw things in the dark. Walk softly through halls you have not cleared.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.13: No champions beaten. Listen: start with the lesser ones, watch their habits, then strike. That is what a Blue Rose does.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.14: The Eye of the Midnight Sun hide behind pretty speeches. Cut through them.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.15: One of the Eye's thorns is pulled. Do not celebrate; there are more.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.16: Spade Kingdom blood magic is petty and cruel. Keep your guard up and your party close.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.17: Lucius turns people into props on his stage. I would very much like to prune him.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.18: More challengers from other worlds. Good. I have been told I am unsociable; this is my chance to be rude to strangers.
arc.dialogue.charlotte_roselei.19: Mind my roses on your way out.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.1: Hi hi hi! I'm Dorothy, Coral Peacock! ...Zzz. Sorry. Mid-hello. It happens.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.2: Welcome to the Sanctuary, %1$s. Have you ever had a dream that felt more real than waking? ...Me neither. Just asking.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.3: Oh, a new face. You look like someone who would share a macaron. ...Yes? Yes.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.4: You're the one in all the dreams lately. Fighting big things. Nice, nice.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.6: You again! Hee hee. I dreamed about you.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.7: In a dream, anything is possible, but it only works if the dreamer is awake enough to hold it. Think about that.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.8: Macarons keep morale up. Strawberry ones especially. This is a fact.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.9: Rest is a weapon, %1$s. If you do not rest properly, you fight worse. I rest properly. All the time.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.10: Cute things are underrated in battle. They make people underestimate you. ...Yawn.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.11: My vice-captain does the paperwork. I do the sleeping. We are very efficient.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.12: I look after my squad, you know. Even when I am asleep. Especially when I am asleep.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.13: Do not worry too much. Worry is just a dream you have with your eyes open.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.14: No champions yet? Mmm. Start with an easy one. Or nap first. Napping first is allowed.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.15: The Eye of the Midnight Sun are so serious. Serious people have terrible dreams. I have seen.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.16: Spade Kingdom dreams are heavy. Like being pushed into a bed that is also a cliff.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.17: Lucius is in a lot of dreams lately. He does not say anything. He just waits. Do not dream about him.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.18: So many worlds in the Chronicle. I dream about them sometimes. Everyone is a little sad and a little hungry. Bring snacks.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.19: Mm. See you. Or I will dream you.
arc.dialogue.dorothy_unsworth.21: Take a nap first. Then go.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.1: I am Fuegoleon Vermillion, captain of the Crimson Lion. Be welcome in the Sanctuary, %1$s.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.2: A delver, then. The dungeon has need of those who keep their heads. Do you?
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.3: Fire is a good servant and a terrible master. I would be glad to see you learn the difference.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.4: Your deeds reached the Sanctuary before you did, %1$s. It is an honour to meet you.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.6: Good to see you on your feet.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.7: A flame with no purpose is only a fire. Decide what you protect, and let the heat follow.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.8: I was struck down once, badly. It taught me what the people behind me are worth. Fight with them, not around them.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.9: The spirit of fire does not lend its power to the careless. Earn it, and take care of it.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.10: My sister Mereoleona has more strength than patience, and my brother Leopold more heart than caution. Between them they keep me humble.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.11: Every boss shows its blow before it lands. A calm eye sees the warning; a hot head sees only the target.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.12: Hold the line together. A party that retreats together can always return.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.13: Start small, %1$s. A guardian on the early floors is still a guardian. There is no shame in bringing company.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.14: The Eye of the Midnight Sun is patient and cruel. Do not let them choose the ground you fight on.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.15: One of the Eye's blades is broken. It is a start, not the end of it.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.16: The Spade Kingdom fights in a way we do not. Do not meet gravity with stubbornness; go around it.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.17: To face Lucius is to face a man who has already thought of your next move. Show him one he has not.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.18: I am told there are warriors in the Chronicle who answer to no kingdom at all. I would be glad to learn from them, and to stand beside them.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.19: Go with fire in your heart and a cool head.
arc.dialogue.fuegoleon_vermillion.21: The Crimson Lion stands behind you.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.1: Hahaha! Look at that, a fresh face! Jack the Ripper, Green Mantis. Don't worry, I only cut things that cut back.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.2: A delver! Good. Delvers always have something worth cutting.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.3: Commoner? Noble? Doesn't matter. Can you swing something sharp? That's all I want to know.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.4: So YOU'RE the one filling the guardians' graves! Come here, let me shake your hand. Carefully.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.5: Hey, it's you! Got anything for me to cut?
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.6: Still alive? Hahaha! I like that.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.7: Everything has a seam. Armour, magic, even the dark between two rooms. Find it and I'll teach you the cut.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.8: Barrier in your way? Cut it. Door in your way? Cut it. Rule in your way... I'll cut that too, if nobody's looking.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.9: Safe Zones are for resting, and resting is for people with somewhere to be. I'm going to sharpen.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.10: Don't mind me licking the blade. It helps me think. It also tastes of victory. Hahaha!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.11: That lazy Black Bull captain keeps calling me a madman. Pot, kettle! Hahaha!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.12: I was born a commoner and I cut just fine. Blood doesn't matter; the edge does. Remember that.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.13: No guardians dead yet? Then you're missing the best part. Go! Hear them crack!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.14: The Eye of the Midnight Sun are lovely targets. Lots of tricks, lots of seams. Tell me how it goes!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.15: Heath Grice? He never liked being cut. Don't blame him. Hahaha!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.16: Gravity, huh? Cut the field itself if you've got the reach. Otherwise... run! Hahaha!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.17: Lucius reads attacks before they land? Then cut fast. Four cuts inside a second, and see how he reads that!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.18: Other worlds, other swords! I hope somebody out there cuts better than I do. Then I can stop being bored.
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.19: Hahaha! Go bring me stories with blood in them!
arc.dialogue.jack_the_ripper.20: Don't get cut! ...Unless it makes a good story.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.1: Ahaha! A new visitor to the Sanctuary! I am Julius Novachrono. Do not stand on ceremony. I certainly do not.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.2: Welcome, %1$s! You have the look of someone who has opened a great many doors and wants to open more. Excellent!
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.3: Ah, so you are the one the dungeon has been whispering about! Come, ask me anything. Time is the one thing I always seem to find.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.4: The records say your story stands at '%3$s', and I am only now learning your name! Forgive a Wizard King his manners.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.6: Back so soon? Or did I wander off in the middle of the hour again? Hee hee.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.7: Every grimoire is a small door. I have spent my life opening them. Never stop reading.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.8: I never judged anyone by rank or by blood. The dungeon does not either: it only asks what you can do.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.9: The Chronicle in the plaza keeps the list of every story told here, and the dungeon plays them back as challengers. Read it before each descent.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.10: Time Magic is mostly patience. Even so, there are moments when patience runs out and only the next breath is left.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.11: Chrono Stasis is the page every Time mage learns to trust. It holds a thing for a few seconds at most. Spend them on a friend's safety, not on greed.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.12: If you find the hours are not enough, I can spare one or two. Not many. Ahaha!
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.13: If a stranger in the plaza gives you good advice, be polite and say thank you. You never know who is wearing a disguise.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.14: Magic is not a ranking. It is a conversation. Listen to your grimoire, and it will tell you what it wants to become.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.15: A champion that falls does not vanish. It joins the Chronicle. That is how we remember them.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.16: Let me tell you how it goes. First the Eye of the Midnight Sun, then the Spade Kingdom, then a name I would rather not say aloud. The Chronicle opens each in its turn.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.17: The Eye of the Midnight Sun is older than the kingdom's quarrels. Their members hold the first guardian floors. Beat them in the order the Chronicle gives.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.18: The devil of the word souls is silenced. One more thread of that old story is cut. Ahaha, I do love a tidy ending!
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.19: The Spade Kingdom now. The Zogratis siblings fight with gravity, blood and bone, and behind them stands a devil whose weight no one bears alone. Bring friends.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.20: The last of them is Lucius Zogratis. He can only be called to his own arena, with the Hourglass of the Final Hour.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.21: Craft the hourglass from gold, a nether star, amethyst, a clock, diamonds and an ender pearl. An odd recipe, but time is odd.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.22: Hold the hourglass, and those within eight paces of you come with you. Choose them well, and do not step in alone.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.23: In that fight a part of me is bound to him. At four moments my will rises, and for a few breaths he is not himself. Strike then, all of you, with everything you have.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.24: He reads the next blow before it falls, unless two of you strike together, or one of you strikes very quickly, or you carry anti-magic. Remember that.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.25: The Chronicle has begun to open pages from other worlds. Seven knights who carry sins, a labyrinth beneath a city called Orario... Stranger and stranger. I am delighted.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.26: If you meet someone from another world, treat them as you would a Magic Knight from another kingdom. Curiosity first. Swords second.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.27: You stood before Lucius and walked away. I... thank you. More than I can say in a single hour.
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.28: Go well, %1$s. And come back with stories!
arc.dialogue.julius_novachrono.29: May your hours be long and your grimoire heavy.
arc.dialogue.kahono.1: Oh! Hello! I'm Kahono, from the Seabed Temple! Well, I used to be. Now I'm from... the sky? The sky is so big!
arc.dialogue.kahono.2: Welcome, %1$s! Songs can close wounds, you know. Mine do. Mostly. I'll sing for you sometime!
arc.dialogue.kahono.3: My brother says I talk too much. Do you think that's true? Don't answer that!
arc.dialogue.kahono.4: You're the one bringing down the champions! Everyone's talking about you! I'm going to write a song about it!
arc.dialogue.kahono.5: %1$s! You came back! I wrote a new verse!
arc.dialogue.kahono.7: If you ever learn Song magic, you can sing it with your own voice! Speak into your microphone, or hold the Sing key if you don't have one.
arc.dialogue.kahono.8: Healing Hymn is for friends, Lullaby for anyone who needs to stop, Barrier Chorus to push foes away, and Requiem for when there is no other way.
arc.dialogue.kahono.9: My Crescendo answers only to my own grimoire. But every other song is yours to learn!
arc.dialogue.kahono.10: I want to be an idol, you know. The first idol of the surface! I think I'd be good at it.
arc.dialogue.kahono.11: My brother Kiato is serious about everything. I'm serious about only a few things. Mostly singing.
arc.dialogue.kahono.12: I've never seen so many stars! Do you have this many where you come from?
arc.dialogue.kahono.13: A song in your head helps in a fight. Hum something! Anything!
arc.dialogue.kahono.14: No champions yet? Then everything is still ahead of you! That's the best kind of song.
arc.dialogue.kahono.15: The Eye of the Midnight Sun frightens me. But we'll face things like that together, right?
arc.dialogue.kahono.16: Vetto is gone? Then Kiato and I can finally breathe. Thank you, thank you!
arc.dialogue.kahono.17: Everyone in the Spade Kingdom looks so sad in the stories. I hope songs can reach them too.
arc.dialogue.kahono.18: Lucius frightens even the captains. So I'll sing the loudest for whoever goes to face him!
arc.dialogue.kahono.19: So many strangers from other worlds in the Chronicle! Imagine the songs they must know!
arc.dialogue.kahono.20: Come back and tell me everything! I'll sing about it!
arc.dialogue.kiato.1: I am Kiato, of the Seabed Temple. The dance is my prayer and my blade. You may call me by name.
arc.dialogue.kiato.2: You walk with purpose. Good. The dance begins with the first step, and so does every journey.
arc.dialogue.kiato.3: Forgive my sister if she talks your ear off. She means well. ...Usually.
arc.dialogue.kiato.4: Your deeds are known even to the Sea God's servants. I am honoured to meet you, %1$s.
arc.dialogue.kiato.7: The dance teaches one thing: be where the blow is not. It sounds simple. It takes a lifetime.
arc.dialogue.kiato.8: A body that moves without fear is harder to strike. Fear tightens; the dance releases.
arc.dialogue.kiato.9: When a missile comes, turn it. When a blow comes, step out. When both come, dance.
arc.dialogue.kiato.10: If you carry the Butoh book, the dance wakes by itself: the body learns to slip out of a blow. Mine is only more practised.
arc.dialogue.kiato.11: My grandfather is the High Priest of the Temple. He taught me that tradition is a river, not a wall.
arc.dialogue.kiato.12: The surface is brighter than I imagined. Kahono sings to the sky every evening. I pretend not to listen.
arc.dialogue.kiato.13: Do not fight the rhythm of a boss. Learn it, and step between its beats.
arc.dialogue.kiato.14: No champions defeated. Begin with patience. Watch the first guardian dance before you join it.
arc.dialogue.kiato.15: The Eye of the Midnight Sun came to our temple once. I will say no more. Defeat them, and the sea grows calmer.
arc.dialogue.kiato.16: Vetto is gone. My sister and I owe you a debt we cannot repay in words.
arc.dialogue.kiato.17: The Spade Kingdom's gravity is a heavy dance. Learn its rhythm, then move where it is not.
arc.dialogue.kiato.18: Lucius reads a fight like a score. Change the tempo.
arc.dialogue.kiato.19: Other worlds have other dances. I would like to learn from their warriors, if they will teach.
arc.dialogue.kiato.21: May the sea carry your steps.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.1: Klaus Lunettes, Golden Dawn. I assume you know what that means. If you do not, you will learn.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.2: State your purpose in the Sanctuary. ...The dungeon, of course. Then listen carefully, because I will say this only once.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.3: A new delver. Tell me, %1$s: do you have a plan, or only courage? Courage is not a plan.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.4: Hm. A delver of record already. Then I will skip the lecture. Mostly.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.5: %1$s. What have you learned since last time?
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.6: Still alive? Good. Dead delvers make poor strategists.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.7: Every dangerous attack shows its warning first: a mark on the floor, a glow, a held breath. Learn the warnings and half the fight is won.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.8: Steel is patient. A wall, a lance, an ally standing behind both. Build a position before you advance.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.9: Do not fight in the open when a corridor will do. Narrow ground favours the prepared.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.10: I was raised to believe nobility is a privilege. I have since learned it is a debt. I intend to repay mine.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.11: Noble or commoner, I judge a mage by how long they stay on their feet. The dungeon keeps the same ledger.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.12: Noise and light draw attention in the dark. Move quietly through halls you have not cleared, and scout before you commit.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.13: No champion defeated, yet you are asking for advice. That alone puts you ahead of most. Study the first guardian's pattern before you commit.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.14: The Eye of the Midnight Sun fights as a unit. When you meet one of them, assume a second plan is hidden behind the first.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.15: You defeated Vetto. A beast with no obvious weakness. I would like your notes, if you kept any.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.16: Gravity, blood, bone. Three siblings, three problems. Solve them one at a time, in the order the Chronicle gives.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.17: Lucius reads a single attacker's rhythm. So break your rhythm, or strike in pairs, or strike so fast he has no time to read.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.18: I cannot evaluate enemies from worlds I have never studied. I will study them anyway. A strategist is paid to be uncomfortable.
arc.dialogue.klaus_lunettes.20: Do nothing unwise. Or, at the least, document it.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.1: Hey! You! I'm Leopold Vermillion, and one day I'll be the strongest of the Vermillions!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.2: Are you a delver? Great! Then we're rivals! Don't argue, it's decided.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.3: Welcome to the Sanctuary! Don't worry, I'll show you around. By which I mean I'll show you how strong I am.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.4: You've beaten champions already?! No way! Then I'll train twice as hard!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.5: Rival! You're back! I've been waiting to show you something!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.6: Oh! It's you! Let's spar sometime!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.7: Fire gets stronger when you shout! ...That might not be true. But it feels true.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.8: My brother is a captain, my sister is a monster, and I'm just getting started. Watch me.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.9: Rest when you're tired and fight when you're not. Even I figured that one out.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.10: Don't just copy someone's spells. Make them yours! That's what my brother says, anyway.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.11: Warm up before the big fights! A stiff arm is a missed block!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.12: No champion yet? Perfect, we start from the same spot, rival! First to beat a guardian wins! ...You're already ahead. I haven't gone yet.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.13: The Eye of the Midnight Sun are tough, but we're tougher! Don't let their tricks scare you, rival!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.14: Heath Grice is beaten? Ha! I would have done it too, just... later!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.15: Spade Kingdom! Gravity! If it pushes you down, push back harder! Or just jump!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.16: Lucius is the last big one? I can't wait! Okay, I can wait a little. I'm a bit scared.
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.17: Rival, there are fighters in the Chronicle from other worlds! Think how strong they must be! I want to fight them all!
arc.dialogue.leopold_vermillion.19: Don't lose to anything without me!
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.1: Marx Francois, aide to the Wizard King. I keep the records of this Sanctuary. You are %1$s, I assume.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.2: I was expecting you, %1$s. The Wizard King announces newcomers before they arrive. Please do not ask how.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.3: Welcome to the Sanctuary. Rule one: nothing in the dungeon is safe. Rule two: everything here is. Do not confuse them.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.4: Your record is already extensive, %1$s. I will need to update several ledgers.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.6: Back again. Good. I dislike unfinished records.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.7: A party is the Magic Knights' oldest tool. Your team shares one chain of floors, and a team's progress belongs to the team.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.8: The System tracks your floor quests and rewards inside the dungeon. Its bonuses sleep outside and wake when you return. Nothing is lost.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.9: Every tenth floor has a Guardian, a Gatekeeper door and a vault. The way on lies behind them. There is no way around.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.10: Safe Zones and Landings are the only places where you recover properly. I record this because people keep dying beside them anyway.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.11: A Canon Grimoire may fall to the first one to defeat a champion, once per world, by chance. Hold it and it lends its skills; put it away and they return.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.12: Champions follow a chain. One opens only when the ones before it have fallen. The Chronicle lists which are open and which are not.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.13: Each floor is a level of its own: you arrive at the foot of a stair and must find the way on. If the stairs say they are still forming, wait. Do not run back.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.14: Wandering champions patrol the halls between the guardian floors. A quiet hall is not an empty one.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.15: Some pages answer only to the grimoire of one particular person. That is by design. Please file it under: not a bug.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.16: I have asked the Wizard King several times to keep a schedule. He says time is not a schedule. I note it for the records.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.17: The records currently place you in: %3$s.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.18: No champions on file. Per protocol, I recommend the lower floors of either road, and a party.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.19: Your current concern is the Eye of the Midnight Sun. Their chain is long. Do not skip links.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.20: Zagred: file closed, pending a review of the aftermath. Please do not reopen it.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.21: The Spade Kingdom files are now open to you. Warning: the Zogratis family uses curses that persist. Do not descend further while marked.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.22: The file on Lucius Zogratis opens only in his arena. Standing order: nobody enters alone. Anyone within reach of the Hourglass bearer travels with them, seven companions at most.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.23: Once the fight has begun, the arena is closed to latecomers, and leaving takes ten seconds. Gather everyone first. I will not be filing a rescue report.
arc.dialogue.marx_francois.24: New files keep arriving from worlds I have not catalogued. I have stopped asking where they come from.
